newsitem.title: DUBAI: First woman seeks to run for president in Iran.
newsitem.headline: First woman seeks to run for president in Iran.

text.p: A female former member of parliament said on Wednesday she would register to run for president of Iran, the first woman to seek the post.
"I am announcing my candidacy because I do not believe there is anything in the Koran or Islam which prevents women from seeking any political office," Azam Taleqani, 54, said.

"I am hoping that my candidacy will lead to a ruling that clarifies that our constitution does not limit the presidency to men," Taleqani, an Islamist political and cultural figure active on women's issues, told Reuters by telephone from Tehran.
Iran's constitution refers to possible candidates with a word which usually means "men" but could also mean "personalities".

Taleqani and a dozen male candidates for the May 23 polls will be screened by the Guardian Council, a body of lawyers and Shi'ite clerics which in past elections disqualified all but a handful of those who sought to run.

Taleqani is the editor of an Islamist women's monthly and runs a women's foundation and a political group. She is a daughter of Ayatollah Mahmoud Taleqani, a prominent clerical leader who died a short time after the 1979 Islamic revolution.
The poll will elect a successor to President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, who is constitutionally barred from running for a third consecutive four-year term.
Iran's highest female official is Shahla Habibi, Rafsanjani's adviser on women's affairs.
